stories.title: Cooke: Potential FAI sanctions remained undetermined
stories.summary: FAI President Paul Cooke admitted after the Republic of Ireland's controversial 3-0 win over Israel that the association were still unclear what additional sanctions they would have potentially faced had they not fulfilled the fixture. The build-up to the game - ever since the draw in February - had been dominated by off-field matters with many calling for Ireland not to take part in response to Israeli attacks on Gaza. The uncertainty over the game prevailed to the very end, with Irish goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu deciding on Saturday that he was not going to play, stating "it would be wrong to participate", before a vote was taken amongst other squad members to see if they would participate. "No," he replied when asked had UEFA threatened any added sanctions if they withdrew from the game and/or the 'home' fixture next Sunday. "The rules are clear. It specifies if we don't fulfil the fixtures what the sanctions are and then there's reference to other sanctions undetermined. "I think it depends on UEFA and what sanctions they levy on somebody as a result of it. We saw a recent thing in England and Southampton, the levies that were levied on them [expelled from the English Championship play-offs after admitting spying on opponents]."

stories.title: Israel captain: 'They hate us, we don't like them'
stories.summary: Israel captain Manor Solomon declared that his country was "ten times better" than Ireland following their Nations League tie in Debrecen, promising a "completely different game" when the sides meet again. The Boys in Green's early dominance decided the game in Nagyerdei Stadion with Troy Parrott, Adam Idah and Jack Moylan scoring goals in that period. The sides are due to meet again in Serbia on Sunday next, with Austria due in Dublin in between, but there are still some question marks remaining over that game in Backa Topola. The Irish players took a vote on Saturday morning to agree to play last night's game, with the majority voting in favour of doing so. At the same time, there was a significant minority opposed to playing, a figure that has not been confirmed by the FAI or manager Heimir Hallgrimsson, but has been reported to be either six or eight players. It remains to be seen whether further discussions amongst the players could see those numbers change.

stories.title: New Leinster Hurling Championship format nears completion
stories.summary: Leinster GAA will this week look to refine their proposal for a new senior inter-county hurling provincial championship of eight teams amid an extended structure. It is hoped that an agreed new format will be reviewed by counties and the Leinster GAA executive and presented before the media in early October. Former GAA president Nickey Brennan is chairing a special workgroup reviewing the structure of the Leinster Senior Hurling Championship to help developing counties achieve more meaningful access to elite competition The aim is to make the Leinster series as competitive as possible and lift developing teams who face steep challenges bridging the gap to higher terrain. From an early stage the plan was always set to consider expanding the current six-team round-robin format into an eight-team competition divided into groups. Factoring in the progress made by 2025 Joe McDonagh Cup champions Kildare – even though they experienced immediate relegation this season – was also a priority for the committee.

stories.title: Snedeker: US team is 'going to be a problem in Ireland'
stories.summary: Victorious Presidents Cup captain Brandt Snedeker believes the United States team "is going to be a problem in Ireland" at next year's Ryder Cup. The 45-year-old received some criticism for his captaincy as they were staring at a first defeat on home soil after being dominated over the first three days at Medinah. However, his players turned things around after winning nine and a half points from the 12 singles matches to eventually prevail 17-13. Snedeker believes that offers hope – although the calibre of opposition did not compare with Luke Donald’s back-to-back winners – for the centenary edition of the Ryder Cup at Adare Manor in Limerick as they bid to win on foreign soil for the first time since 1993. "It doesn’t mean anything for me, it means more for USA golf," he said. "I think we’re all tired of this narrative that we don’t care about each other, that we don’t know how to play team golf. I think this proves it.

stories.title: Leading fancies stand their ground in Arc
stories.summary: A total of 19 horses remain in the Qatar Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe at ParisLongchamp following Monday's first forfeit stage. They include last year's winner Daryz for Francis-Henri Graffard and the William Haggas-trained Maltese Cross, who was runner-up in the Epsom Derby and won the Grand Prix de Paris over the Arc course and distance. Graffard and the Aga Khan Studs have an interesting second string to their bow in the shape of Prix Niel scorer Varandir, whose only defeat to date came in the Grand Prix de Paris, for which he was favourite. Kalpana has stood her ground for Andrew Balding after a stellar season highlighted by victory in the King George VI And Queen Elizabeth Stakes, with English Oaks heroine Thundering On remaining in contention for Joseph O'Brien. Diamond Necklace is one of three for Aidan O'Brien, along with Benvenuto Cellini and Minnie Hauk, who found only Daryz too good 12 months ago. Runaway Coronation Cup winner Bay City Roller is still in for George Scott, while Roger Varian has recent German Group One winner Saddadd engaged.

stories.title: McMillan: Work needed to get Munster fans back on side
stories.summary: Munster head coach Clayton McMillan says he and his players have to "work" to get some supporters back on board, but the New Zealander is confident with their direction of travel, despite Saturday's 26-20 defeat to Glasgow Warriors. The province let a 20-14 lead slip in the final quarter at Thomond Park, as they lost what McMillan described as an "arm-wrestle" against a powerful Scottish side. Despite the defeat, there were clear positives in the performance, notably through 21-year-old scrum-half Ben O'Donovan, and new signing Kieran Brookes. A modest crowd of just over 11,000 turned up at Thomond Park for what should have been an attractive fixture, with a 5.30pm kick-off against one of the league's best sides. And the Munster coach acknowledged they are in the process of repairing the relationship with some fans after a chaotic season last year. "I think for the people that were here, I hope that they saw something in the team to be optimistic about," McMillan (below) said on Saturday night.

stories.title: Hallgrimsson: 'In tough times, you find your leaders'
stories.summary: Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson hailed the character of his squad after they dismantled Israel 3-0 in a hugely controversial encounter in Debrecen and said that some of the commentary attacking the squad had gone too far in recent days. First half goals from Troy Parrott, Adam Idah and Jack Moylan saw the Republic of Ireland bounce back from defeat in Pristina to put Israel to the sword with surprising ease in a game which was almost boycotted by the Irish squad after Gavin Bazunu's late withdrawal in protest at the "atrocities in the region" led to a four-hour debate among the squad on Saturday. The squad eventually voted to proceed with the fixture - which had been preceded by months of protests and calls for a boycott. "It's been tough times for them, and I think everybody that has watched the game saw proud Irishmen fight for their nation. "I think they show how much this means to them, not only to play for Ireland, but to do well tonight under a difficult circumstance, with a bad preparation. Just to be able to do that, I'm so proud of them." The starting team saw five changes to the team which lost in Kosovo, with both Liam Scales and Finn Azaz being left out of the side.

stories.title: Alleged racism against Idah will not be investigated
stories.summary: An alleged racist incident involving Ireland goalscorer Adam Idah will not be investigated by UEFA because it wasn't explicitly mentioned on the pitch. The Boys in Green delivered a 3-0 victory in their controversial Nations League fixture against Israel in Debrecen. During the first half, Jayson Molumby asked match referee Harms Osmers and the fourth official Florian Exner to listen to alleged monkey chants from the tiny number of supporters in the stadium in what was officially an 'away' fixture for Heimir Hallgrimsson's side. According to reports, UEFA said that Molumby had not explicitly mentioned racism to the officials, and that officials had not heard any of the chanting taking place. As such, because the incident was not reported as racism on the pitch, the governing body's protocols mean that no action can be taken.

stories.title: First-half goals see Ireland past Israel in Debrecen
stories.summary: The Republic of Ireland picked up their first win of the UEFA Nations League campaign after beating Israel 3-0 in a controversial fixture at the Nagyerdei Stadion in Debrecen, Hungary. First-half goals from Troy Parrott, Adam Idah and Jack Moylan proved enough for Heimir Hallgrimsson's side to take all three points, after losing their opener in Kosovo 1-0 on Thursday. The match in Debrecen was played out in front of a limited attendance inside the 20,340-seater venue. As had been confirmed in Saturday's pre-match press conference, the Irish team entered the pitch wearing black armbands in recognition of "all lives lost in the conflict". During the Israeli anthem, they bowed their heads and there were no handshakes between the sets of players afterwards, nor between captains Dara O’Shea and Manor Solomon. Kick-off at the Nagyerdei Stadion followed a tense day in Debrecen on its eve. On Saturday morning, the scheduled press conference and training session was postponed shortly before it was due to start.

stories.title: Healy finishes 10th in road race world championships
stories.summary: Ireland's Ben Healy came home in 10th place in an impressive showing in the road race world championships in Montreal, in which Brandon McNulty of the United States emerged as the surprise winner. Healy was unable to replicate his bronze medal showing in last year's race but was well in contention among the leading pack but fell away in the closing stages. The 28-year-old McNulty put his hands on his helmet in disbelief and pumped his fist after crossing the finish line with a time of 6 hours, 17 minutes and 4 seconds. Australia's Michael ‌Matthews was second and Mathieu van der Poel of the Netherlands was third.McNulty, who won the Montreal Grand Prix last year, launched his attack with 32 km to go and held a ‌50-second lead heading into the final lap. He struggled on the last significant climb and saw his lead shrink to ‌10 seconds with 10 km left but none of the ‌chasers were able to take advantage, with Van der Poel leading an attack with 6.8 km to go that fizzled out. The absence of two-time defending champion Tadej Pogacar, who is recovering from a crash he suffered last month, left the field open.The last American man to win the elite road race world title was Lance Armstrong in 1993.

stories.title: NFL: Washington Commanders end Seattle's winning run
stories.summary: Marcus Mariota threw three touchdown passes as the Washington Commanders claimed a 33-31 victory over Seattle to end the Seahawks' long winning streak. Seattle had won a dozen games in a row, following up last season’s Super Bowl triumph by starting their campaign with back-to-back triumphs, but Mariota starred in the absence of the injured Jayden Daniels. Also crucial in the Commanders’ first win of the season was Kain Medrano intercepting Sam Darnold’s pass and sprinting 50 yards for a touchdown as Seattle tasted defeat for the first time since November. Chris Boswell kicked the go-ahead field goal as the Pittsburgh Steelers bounced back from their defeat to the New England Patriots by edging out the Cincinnati Bengals 30-27. The Bengals’ hopes of avoiding a first defeat of the season ended when Joe Burrow fumbled in the final minute after being strip-sacked by Derrick Harmon. Trevor Lawrence threw touchdown passes for Josh Cameron, Jakobi Meyers and Parker Washington to lift the Jacksonville Jaguars to an impressive 35-6 win over the Patriots.

stories.title: Shels win FAI Cup to shatter Athlone's double dreams
stories.summary: Shelbourne produced a brilliantly efficient performance to win the Club Orange Women's FAI Cup and shatter Athlone Town's dreams of doing the double-double. Athlone were crowned league champions last night after Galway United were beaten by Wexford. But they were picked apart by their old rivals at Tallaght Stadium. Shels were outstanding in the opening period, plundering three goals through the eye-catching Halle Harcourt, Alex Kavanagh and Maeve Wollmer. There was no way back for Athlone, Hannah Waesch's fine strike just too little too late, though they did have their chances, and will curse poor finishing and the excellence of keeper Mya Sanchez when they reflect on this decider. Conditions were good in Tallaght: a light breeze, mild temperatures and autumn sunshine. The shadow of events in Debrecen hung over the pre-match fanfare. Shels supporters produced a 'Stop The Game' flag, and a banner that read: 'Bazunu Abu, the voice of justice'.

stories.title: Parsons: History on home soil is 'really special'
stories.summary: In two Tests at Dexcom Stadium, Beibhinn Parsons has crossed for five Ireland tries, and this afternoon's two against Japan in Galway sent the winger into the record books. The Galway native's brace in Ireland's 31-24 win brought her to 24 tries in green, first matching and then surpassing the previous record held for several years by Alison Miller. And doing it on home soil was the cherry on top of the day for the Ballinasloe native. "It's just really special to be in Galway and have all my family be here," Parsons said after seven-point win. "I don't even think they're aware of it. It's not something that I'd really talk about. So, yeah, it's just special to play at home." Still only 24-years-old, Parsons international tally is only going to grow over the next few years, achieving the feat across just 37 caps.

stories.title: US dominate singles to seal another Presidents Cup win
stories.summary: The United States had their own Medinah moment after overturning a three-point deficit to retain the Presidents Cup by beating Geoff Ogilvy's International Team 17-13. Brandt Snedeker’s USA trailed 10.5-7.5 but – much like Europe in their famous comeback at the same venue in the 2012 Ryder Cup, dubbed the 'Miracle at Medinah’ – they were resurgent in the singles on the final day. Cameron Young, Justin Thomas and Scottie Scheffler all won early on, although Tom Kim and Sungjae Im hit back to leave the Internationals needing three more points for a first triumph since 1998. But wins for Chris Gotterup, Patrick Cantlay and Collin Morikawa put the USA ahead and Jacob Bridgeman claimed the point that sealed the win, fighting back from one down with three to play to overcome Min Woo Lee on the final hole. After holding his nerve from three and a half feet, Bridgeman said: "I heard someone in the crowd say ‘you’re the best putter in the world’. "I was standing over a four-footer and I’m like, this is cake. This is so easy. I’m just so proud I could put it away for the team."

stories.title: Austria make it two wins from two against Kosovo
stories.summary: Austria made it two wins from two in Group 3 of UEFA Nations League B after a 3-1 win over Kosovo at the Ernst-Happel-Stadion in Vienna. Ralf Rangnick's side won by the same scoreline against Israel in Thursday's opener but required two additional time goals from Phillipp Mwene and Sasa Kalajdzic. There was no such drama this time as they eased past a Kosovo side that had proved too strong for the Republic of Ireland in their own opening fixture. In the first ever meeting between the two nations, the visitors nearly hit the front in the opening minutes through their dangerman Vedat Muriqi, but the Fenerbahce man scooped over when he looked certain to score after the ball fell kindly to him in the box. Kosovo were made to pay when Austria hit the front 23 minutes in. Romano Schmid's free-kick into the box was met by the head of David Affengruber, his looping effort leaving Arijanet Muric flat-footed in what was his first goal for his country - awarded after a VAR check for offside.

stories.title: Nishimura takes first LPGA title
stories.summary: Japan's Yuna Nishimura picked up her first LPGA title after a five-stroke victory at the Walmart NW Arkansas Championship. A pair of 63s saw Nishimura take control of the 54-hole tournament with a final-round 66 ensuring a 21-under par score, five clear of a trio of players. That group in joint second included In-Gee Chun, Chanettee Wannasaen and Akie Iwai who stormed up the leaderboard after a sensational closing 62. Ireland's Lauren Walsh finished just outside the top 50 with a Sunday round of 70 leaving her on five-under par. Stephanie Meadow and Leona Maguire were cut after two rounds at Pinnacle Country Club.

stories.title: Nations League: Wales come unstuck against Denmark
stories.summary: Wales wilted in Copenhagen as a 2-0 defeat to Denmark left them bottom of their Nations League group. After a first half in which Wales were very much second best and fortunate to reach the break level, Denmark's domination was rewarded by a Ben Davies own goal and a Gustav Isaksen strike. Wales lost Thursday’s opener to Portugal 1-0 and it leaves them without a point - and a goal - in Group A4, and already facing an uphill battle to avoid relegation. Denmark were under similar pressure after being beaten by Norway on Thursday, but rose to the occasion and should have won more comfortably. The home side thought they had taken the lead in the 24th minute. Wales were exposed by a counter-attack led by Mikkel Damsgaard and Isaksen met Rasmus Hojlund's cross with a thumping volley, only for VAR to rule offside in the build-up. They did move ahead in the second half. Damsgaard delivered a delicious ball and although Hojlund wheeled away celebrating the final touch, it seemed as though it would go down against the unfortunate Davies.

stories.title: Fitzpatrick finishes the job to win Open de France
stories.summary: Matt Fitzpatrick claimed Open de France glory with a final round of 70 to win by three shots at Le Golf National. The 32-year-old Englishman put himself in pole position on Saturday by matching Seve Ballesteros' 1985 record for the lowest 54-hole score at continental Europe’s oldest tournament, reaching 19 under ahead of Sunday’s final round. With a five-shot advantage over home favourite Tom Vaillant, a solid front nine put world number four Fitzpatrick within touching distance of a first DP World Tour title of the season – and an 11th overall – despite a flurry of birdies for Eugenio Lopez-Chacarra. Any chance of a dramatic finale quickly disappeared with a birdie at the 13th for Fitzpatrick and, even though another on 15th was followed by a bogey to close, the 2022 US Open champion was able to toast a special victory in Paris. Spain’s Angel Hidalgo ended up as Fitzpatrick’s nearest challenger after carding 67 to finish on 17 under, with Vaillant one of four players tied for third on 15 under alongside Lopez-Chacarra. This was Fitzpatrick’s fourth tournament victory of 2026, having triumphed on the PGA Tour at the Valspar Championship, RBC Heritage and Zurich Classic of New Orleans.

stories.title: Parsons breaks record as Ireland hold off Japan in Galway
stories.summary: Beibhinn Parsons became Ireland's record tryscorer, as Scott Bemand's side returned to winning ways in the WXV Global Series. The Galway native scored two tries on home soil at Dexcom Stadium to bring her Test tally to 24 for Ireland, on a day where Ireland just about had enough to edge a 31-24 win against a plucky Japan side. Bemand's side scored five tries in total, with Brittany Hogan also crossing twice, with one for Aoife Dalton, but several of the issues from last week's defeat to USA were again on display. Ireland were 19-0 in front approaching half time before their indiscipline allowed the opposition back into the game; Erin King picking up a yellow card and Japan scored two tries during that period, while they gave away a total of 16 penalties across the 80 minutes. Maul defence will also be a concern ahead of next week's rematch with Japan in Cork, as the Sakura XV used that avenue to score three of their four tries. While those issues will be a concern, Ireland's ability to grind through the second half will be a big positive, particularly into such a strong wind, while their scrum was largely dominant as they used Eilís Cahill and Linda Djougang to real effect, with Anna McGann exceptional in the centre.

stories.title: Tension and toxicity after extraordinary day in Hungary
stories.summary: At the end of one of the most extraordinarily tense days in Irish football history, the Republic of Ireland will take the field in Debrecen to play Israel in the Nations League this evening. After months of protests and rancour, it appeared that an unlikely boycott could be in the offing at the eleventh hour after Ireland's Saturday morning press conference and training session were sensationally postponed. Having agreed to proceed from Pristina to Debrecen following a meeting on Friday, it emerged that one player was having grave doubts and wished to withdraw. The Irish Independent's Daniel McDonnell was the first to report that Gavin Bazunu was the player in question. This sparked a four-hour long player meeting, as the Irish media contingent decamped to the team base at the Mercure Hotel. Those who can recall Ireland's last World Cup appearance will have gotten flashbacks to Saipan and the sense of a fast-moving crisis unfolding behind closed meeting room doors, accompanied by a drip-feed of rumours relayed to the waiting media outside. Though given the tragic backdrop, this particular episode is unlikely to be the subject of a breezy tragicomic film in a couple of decades time.

stories.summary: Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson said "we are here to play football" ahead of the UEFA Nations League clash with Israel in Hungary tonight. The Irish team were at the Nagyerdei Stadion in Debrecen at 6pm after a chaotic 48 hours which had seen the fixture put in doubt. The game started at 7.45pm after debate raged for months over whether it should be played. The Irish players did not shake hands with the Israeli players and bowed their heads during the Israeli national anthem. Ireland will play Israel again next week, as well as Austria in Dublin on Thursday. Hallgrimsson has chosen his team for tonight's fixture with Gavin Bazunu not in the squad after yesterday’s withdrawal.

stories.title: Alexander follows up Irish Open triumph in Italy
stories.summary: This year's KPMG Women's Irish Open champion Casandra Alexander has won the Ladies Italian Open by a three-shot margin, while Sara Byrne was the only Irish player in action on Sunday, finishing tied for 23rd. A month after clinching a wire-to-wire victory at the K Club, South African Alexander had shared the lead after Friday's opening night at Golf Club Milano and after a 68 on Saturday, remained tied at the summit with Sweden's Moa Folke and Germany’s Alexandra Forsterling going into the final round. A three-under 69 on Sunday, including an eagle on nine to wipe out a double bogey and bogey on two and five respectively, was enough for her to finish on 12 under and hold off Anna Morgan and Sophie Hausmann, who finished three adrift after posting a 69 and 64 respectively. "I'm glad I didn’t have to wait for this one as long as I waited for the previous one," said Alexander. "My game’s in the right place to win golf tournaments, so I’m looking forward to the rest of the season and having more opportunities. As golfers, as soon as you get one, you’re after the next one, so I’m really happy to walk away with the win and it’s great to be here in Italy." Meanwhile, Cork native Byrne also carded a 69 to finish just outside the top 20 on two under.
